newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends down, makes new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends down, makes new contract lows.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures ended lower Friday and all months made new contract lows as the market fell in tandem with soybeans, traders said.
Soymeal futures also ended lower, and volume in both pits was described by floor sources as light.
"It was really thin in there (soyoil pit)," said one trader. "A 30-lot could move the market five ticks."

Soybeans set a bearish tone for soymeal and soyoil futures on Friday. Soybeans fell on forecasts showing ideal, or warm and rainy, weather for much of the U.S. Midwest through the weekend, traders said.
The lower prices in soyoil generated talk that U.S. soyoil exporters were receiving active price enquiries from Chinese buyers, floor sources said.
"I think we're getting competitive in the world markets finally," said a soy complex trader.
July soyoil fell to the lowest level for a nearby contract since January 3.
July soymeal settled down $3.00 per ton at $270.90, and other months were down $0.80 to $2.50. July soyoil closed down 0.19 cent a lb at 22.85 cents, and other months were 0.09 to 0.35 lower.
July soyoil set a fresh contract low of 22.75 cents and December set a new low of 23.23 cents. All other months also set new lows.
Soymeal futures derived some support from talk that China bought 125,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for July/August delivery, but no confirmation of the trades could be obtained.
"I can't understand any processor wanting to price soymeal now for August," said one crusher.
On Friday after the close, ADM confirmed that it would cut back soybean crushing operations because of falling crush margins and tight supplies.
In soymeal trade, Continental Grain sold 300 lots July and Merrill Lynch sold 200 July, trades said. Term Commodities bought 200 July, pit sources said.
In soyoil trade, ADM bought 100 lots July, 100 August, 100 September and 100 October and Merrill Lynch sold 100 December and 100 August, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 20,955 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 21,000 lots, against Thursday's 15,469.
